patient_vignette: A 67-year-old man presents after a transperineal biopsy confirmed acinar adenocarcinoma of the prostate, Gleason 4+3=7, with PSA 14.8 ng/mL and cancer in 6 of 12 cores. He has no bone pain or urinary retention, and his exam is otherwise unremarkable. His urologist is discussing radical prostatectomy versus radiation-based treatment, and the team notes that local staging would help with counseling, although the patient is leaning strongly toward definitive radiotherapy regardless of nerve-sparing considerations. He is otherwise fit and wants treatment, but the surgeon does not expect imaging to change the operative plan.

Rule ID: R001
Scenario: PREOP_STAGING
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: Newly diagnosed biopsy-confirmed prostate cancer; intermediate- or high-risk; being considered for radical therapy; knowledge of extraprostatic extension would alter management
Guideline Action: Consider multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) for pre-treatment local staging to assess extraprostatic extension (EPE).
Source Statement: Multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) use for pre-treatment local staging of prostate cancer is a reasonable option for assessment of extraprostatic extension (EPE) in intermediate-and highrisk patients being considered for radical therapy if knowledge of EPE will alter management.

patient_vignette: A 67-year-old man presents after a transrectal biopsy confirmed acinar adenocarcinoma of the prostate, Gleason 3+4=7, with PSA 14.8 ng/mL and cancer in 2 of 12 cores. He has no bone pain or urinary retention, and his exam is otherwise unremarkable. His urologist is discussing active surveillance versus focal therapy, and the team is considering whether local staging might help define the extent of disease. He is otherwise fit and wants to avoid immediate radical treatment if possible. A pelvic MRI from 3 months ago was done for unrelated hip pain and showed only mild degenerative changes, with no dedicated prostate sequences.

patient_vignette: A 62-year-old man was diagnosed with symptomatic multiple myeloma 10 months ago after presenting with anemia, lytic bone lesions, and elevated serum protein. He completed induction therapy followed by a single autologous stem cell transplant. He recovered well and has good functional status with no major comorbidities. At follow-up, his marrow and labs show a very good partial response, and there is no evidence of progressive disease. He asks whether he should receive another transplant now to improve long-term control.
rules_text:
Rule ID: R001
Scenario: INITIAL_DIAGNOSIS
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: Adult patient with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma being considered for initial transplant-based treatment
Guideline Action: Offer autologous stem cell transplantation as part of the initial treatment plan.
Source Statement: Autologous SCT is the recommended treatment option for patients with newly diagnosed MM, as part of the initial treatment plan.

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: INITIAL_DIAGNOSIS
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: Newly diagnosed MM patient is free from severe comorbidities and younger than 65 years after initial high-dose chemotherapy
Guideline Action: Offer a single autologous stem cell transplant.
Source Statement: Evidence included in four Clinical Practice Guidelines (CPGs) (1)(2)(3)(4) suggests that a single transplant with autologous SCT should be offered to all MM patients who are free from severe co-morbidities and who are younger than 65 years of age, following the initial treatment with high-dose chemotherapy.

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: TREATMENT_RESPONSE
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: Patient did not achieve complete remission after initial autologous SCT
Guideline Action: Offer a second autologous stem cell transplant.
Source Statement: Evidence included in two CPGs (1,2) suggests that double autologous SCT should be offered to patients who did not achieve a complete remission after their initial autologous SCT.

Rule ID: R004
Scenario: RECURRENCE_OR_RESTAGING
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: Patient relapses after a long remission following a single transplant
Guideline Action: Offer a second autologous transplant.
Source Statement: ...the SCT Steering Committee's consensus opinion is that patients who relapse after a long remission following a single transplant should be offered a second transplant.

Rule ID: R005
Scenario: INITIAL_DIAGNOSIS
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: Newly diagnosed MM patient is age 65 or older but has good performance status and no comorbidities that contraindicate transplantation
Guideline Action: Consider offering autologous stem cell transplantation.
Source Statement: The SCT Steering Committee acknowledged that, while the evidence upon which the CPGs were based almost uniformly excluded patients older than age 65, there was no reason not to offer SCT to patients 65 or older who have good performance status and no co-morbidities that would be a contraindication to transplantation.

Rule ID: R006
Scenario: TREATMENT_RESPONSE
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: Patient with MM responds to first autologous transplant with less than a very good partial response and has no progressive disease

Scenario: TREATMENT_RESPONSE
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: Patient has high-risk MM
Guideline Action: Consider allogeneic transplantation, preferably within an investigative study.
Source Statement: Allogeneic transplantation is an option for patients with high-risk MM preferably within the context of an investigative study.

Rule ID: R008
Scenario: TREATMENT_RESPONSE
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: Patient with high-risk MM is younger than 50 years and is not expected to benefit from autologous SCT

Contrast CT shows a 2.8 cm mass in the pancreatic head with mild biliary dilation, but the lesion is still indeterminate on imaging. Endoscopic ultrasound-guided biopsy is attempted twice and is nondiagnostic due to scant tissue. He has no known metastatic disease, and the surgical team is considering whether he could be a candidate for potentially curative resection if the diagnosis is confirmed. The oncology team asks whether PET/CT should be used next to help clarify the diagnosis and guide management.

Scenario: INITIAL_DIAGNOSIS
Priority: 80

MRI shows a new enhancing lesion near the prior resection cavity, but the findings are equivocal for either tumor recurrence or radiation necrosis. His oncology team is considering PET/CT to help clarify the diagnosis before changing therapy. He has no fever, seizures, or other signs of infection, and his neurologic exam is otherwise stable. The main question is whether the new imaging abnormality represents recurrent tumor or treatment-related necrosis.

Rule ID: R001
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: all patients with endometrial cancer after potentially curative primary treatment and no evidence of disease
Guideline Action: counsel about potential symptoms of recurrence
Source Statement: It is recommended that all patients receive counselling about the potential symptoms of recurrence of endometrial cancer, because the majority of recurrences in the identified studies were symptomatic.

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: patient is surgically or pathologically confirmed low risk of recurrence (stage IA or IB, grade 1 or 2)
Guideline Action: perform general examination including complete history and pelvic-rectal examination semi-annually or annually for the first 3 years, then annually for the next 2 years
Source Statement: For patients at a surgically or pathologically confirmed low risk of recurrence (i.e., stage IA or IB, grade 1 or 2): A general examination, including a complete history and a pelvicrectal examination, conducted semi-annually or annually for the first three years and annually for the next two years.

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: patient is high risk of recurrence (stage IA or IB, grade 3, or stage IC or advanced stage)
Guideline Action: perform general examination including complete history and pelvic-rectal examination every 3 to 6 months for the first 3 years, then semi-annually for the next 2 years
Source Statement: For patients at high risk of recurrence (i.e., stage IA or IB, grade 3, or stage IC or advanced stage). A general examination, including a complete history and a pelvic-rectal examination, every three to six months for the first three years and semi-annually for the next two years.

Rule ID: R004
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: planning follow-up setting or specialist type for any patient
Guideline Action: follow the patient with a health care professional knowledgeable about the natural history of the disease and comfortable performing speculum and pelvic exams
Source Statement: There is insufficient evidence to inform the optimum clinical setting or type of specialist required for follow-up; however, it is recommended that all patients be followed by a health care professional who is knowledgeable about the natural history of the disease, and who is comfortable performing speculum and pelvic exams, in order to diagnose or detect a local (vaginal) recurrence.

Rule ID: R005
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: patient has symptoms suggestive of recurrence
Guideline Action: perform targeted investigation to rule out recurrence
Source Statement: It is recommended that all patients undergo a targeted investigation to rule out recurrence if symptomatic, since patients with local recurrence are potentially curable with further therapy.

Rule ID: R006
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: treatment includes radiotherapy
Guideline Action: counsel the patient on potential adverse effects of radiotherapy
Source Statement: Where treatment with radiotherapy is involved, it is recommended that patients be counselled on the potential adverse effects of radiotherapy.

Rule ID: R007
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: all patients with endometrial cancer after potentially curative primary treatment and no evidence of disease
Guideline Action: use a follow-up strategy based on recurrence risk and patient preferences
Source Statement: The most appropriate follow-up strategy is likely one based upon the risk of recurrence, with individual patient preferences for more or less follow-up taken into account.

Rule ID: R008
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: patient has remained recurrence-free for 5 years
Guideline Action: return to annual population-based general physical and pelvic examination
Source Statement: Since the majority of patients with recurrence were symptomatic and virtually all recurred within five years, it seems reasonable that patients return to annual population-based general physical and pelvic examination after five years of recurrence-free follow-up.

Activation Condition: patient with completely resected cutaneous melanoma outside a clinical trial

Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: patient with completely resected cutaneous melanoma

patient_vignette: A 63-year-old man with progressive dysphagia to solids and a 7-kg weight loss is diagnosed with a mid-thoracic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma on endoscopy and biopsy. Staging CT and PET show no distant metastases, and endoscopic ultrasound suggests a locally advanced but resectable tumor with preserved performance status. Thoracic surgery feels he is an appropriate candidate for esophagectomy after neoadjuvant treatment. He has well-controlled hypertension and no major cardiopulmonary disease. In clinic, he asks whether he can proceed directly to surgery or if treatment before surgery would improve his chances. The oncology team is considering preoperative therapy options and discussing expected toxicities and the fact that any survival benefit may be modest. The patient says he values the best chance of cure but wants to understand how treatment might affect swallowing, fatigue, and recovery before making a decision.

Scenario: INITIAL_DIAGNOSIS
Priority: 80

Priority: 70

Activation Condition: Adult patient has resectable, operable, potentially curable thoracic esophageal cancer and surgery is appropriate
Guideline Action: Use preoperative platinum-based chemotherapy plus radiotherapy as the preferred treatment modality
Source Statement: Preoperative cisplatin-based chemotherapy plus radiotherapy is recommended as the preferred modality for the management of surgically resectable patients with esophageal cancer.

Scenario: INITIAL_DIAGNOSIS
Priority: 60

Scenario: INITIAL_DIAGNOSIS
Priority: 60

Source Statement: Based on the majority of the evidence available at this time, the GI DSG believes that preoperative chemoradiotherapy for resectable carcinoma of the esophagus is the preferred approach.

patient_vignette: A 58-year-old woman with ER-positive breast cancer presents with worsening deep aching pain in her pelvis and lower back. Imaging shows multiple lytic bone metastases without spinal cord compression. She is already receiving denosumab for skeletal-related event prevention. rules_text:
Rule ID: R001
Scenario: INITIAL_DIAGNOSIS
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: Biopsy-naive patient at elevated risk of clinically significant prostate cancer and a candidate for curative management with suspected clinically localized prostate cancer
Guideline Action: Perform multiparametric MRI prior to biopsy
Source Statement: MPMRI is recommended prior to biopsy in patients who are candidates for curative management with suspected clinically localized prostate cancer.

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: INITIAL_DIAGNOSIS
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: Biopsy-naive patient has a positive multiparametric MRI
Guideline Action: Perform multiparametric MRI-targeted biopsy together with transrectal ultrasound systematic biopsy
Source Statement: If the MPMRI is positive, MPMRI-TB and TRUS-SB should be performed together to maximize detection of CSPCa.

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: RECURRENCE_OR_RESTAGING
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: Patient had a prior negative transrectal ultrasound systematic biopsy and is at high risk of clinically significant prostate cancer with curative management being considered
Guideline Action: Perform multiparametric MRI
Source Statement: In patients who had a prior negative TRUS-SB and demonstrate a high risk of having CSPCa in whom curative management is being considered: MPMRI should be performed,

Rule ID: R004
Scenario: RECURRENCE_OR_RESTAGING
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: Patient had a prior negative transrectal ultrasound systematic biopsy and multiparametric MRI is positive
Guideline Action: Perform targeted biopsy
Source Statement: If the MPMRI is positive, targeted biopsy should be performed.

Rule ID: R005
Scenario: INITIAL_DIAGNOSIS
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: Biopsy-naive patient has a negative multiparametric MRI
Guideline Action: Consider forgoing biopsy after discussing risks and benefits with the patient and arranging ongoing follow-up
Source Statement: If the MPMRI is negative, consider forgoing any biopsy after discussion of the risks and benefits with the patient as part of shared decision making and ongoing followup.

Rule ID: R006
Scenario: INITIAL_DIAGNOSIS

Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: Biopsy-naive patient has a negative multiparametric MRI
Guideline Action: Inform the patient that a negative multiparametric MRI may miss clinically significant prostate cancer
Source Statement: Between 8% and 24% of patients with CSPCa may be missed by a negative MPMRI.

Scenario: INITIAL_DIAGNOSIS
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: Considering multiparametric MRI for a biopsy-naive patient
Guideline Action: Use multiparametric MRI only if high-quality interpretation is available and operators have experience performing targeted biopsies
Source Statement: MPMRI should only be performed if there is availability of high-quality MPMRI interpretation and operators with experience performing targeted biopsies (see Recommendation 3).

Source Statement: Due to the limited availability, MPMRI is recommended only for patients where there is intent of curative management should the biopsy be positive for CSPCa.

Core biopsy confirms intermediate-grade DCIS. Breast imaging shows a 2.1 cm localized area without multifocal disease, and the breast surgeon feels she is a good candidate for breast-conserving surgery. She asks about treatment options and whether radiation would still be needed after surgery.

The hospital notes that the case would be done by a fellowship-trained gynecologic oncologist, but this is the center’s first vulvar SLNB case and it has not yet built a local SLNB follow-up program.

Rule ID: R001
Scenario: INITIAL_DIAGNOSIS
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: clinically suspicious groin nodes are present
Guideline Action: do not perform SLNB
Source Statement: SLNB is not recommended when there are clinically suspicious groin nodes.

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: considering blue dye alone for SLNB mapping
Guideline Action: do not use blue dye alone
Source Statement: Blue dye alone should be discouraged because of its low detection rate.

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: considering use of blue dye alone because of low detection rate
Guideline Action: avoid blue dye alone
Source Statement: Blue dye alone should be discouraged because of its low detection rate.

Rule ID: R004
Scenario: INITIAL_DIAGNOSIS
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: woman with unifocal vulvar squamous cell tumour smaller than 4 cm and clinically nonsuspicious groin nodes
Guideline Action: perform sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB)
Source Statement: SLNB is recommended for women with unifocal tumours <4 cm in size and clinically nonsuspicious nodes in the groin.

Rule ID: R005
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: performing SLNB for early-stage vulvar cancer
Guideline Action: ensure appropriate surgical training with supervised SLNB experience, complete IFLD follow-up without false negatives, and ongoing annual experience
Source Statement: Appropriate surgical training (i.e., supervised experiences with SLNB procedures followed by complete IFLD without any false negatives and ongoing annual experience with cases to maintain competence) is recommended to optimize patient outcomes and safety.

Rule ID: R006
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: performing SLNB for early-stage vulvar cancer
Guideline Action: have the procedure performed by gynecologic oncologists in Gynecologic Oncology Centres
Source Statement: This procedure should be performed by gynecologic oncologists in Gynecologic Oncology Centres.

Rule ID: R007
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: centre performing SLNB for vulvar cancer
Guideline Action: ensure at least 10 successful SLNB followed by IFLD cases per centre
Source Statement: Although volume has not been explicitly studied, the Working Group agrees that successful experience with SLNB followed by IFLD in at least 10 patients per centre is recommended.

Rule ID: R008
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: performing SLNB mapping
Guideline Action: use radiocolloid tracers alone or with blue dye
Source Statement: Radiocolloid tracers should be used alone or with blue dye.

patient_vignette: A 59-year-old man with a recently diagnosed mid-rectal adenocarcinoma is being evaluated for possible neoadjuvant treatment. He has mild intermittent rectal bleeding but no bowel obstruction. On digital rectal exam, the tumor is palpable on the posterior rectal wall, about 7 cm from the anal verge, with reduced mobility. The oncology team is considering preoperative chemoradiation because the lesion may be locally advanced, but the staging workup is not yet complete. He has had no dedicated pelvic MRI, no endorectal ultrasound, and no CT of the abdomen or chest imaging. The patient asks whether the tumor is definitely stage III, and the team explains that preoperative staging can be imperfect and the final extent may differ from initial tests.

rules_text:
Rule ID: R001
Scenario: PREOP_STAGING
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: Before preoperative therapy is planned
Guideline Action: Perform adequate preoperative staging investigations including transrectal ultrasound and/or MRI for T category, MRI for N category, digital rectal exam, CT or MRI to assess mesorectal margin, CT or MRI of the abdomen for metastatic or stage IV disease, and chest x-ray for pulmonary imaging.
Source Statement: Recommendations for preoperative therapy presuppose adequate preoperative staging investigations, including transrectal ultrasound and/or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with surface or endorectal coil to assess the T category, MRI with surface or endorectal coil to assess the N category, a good digital rectal exam, computerized axial tomography (CAT) scan or MRI to assess the mesorectal margin, CAT scan or MRI of the abdomen to assess for potential metastatic or stage IV disease, and chest x-ray for pulmonary imaging.

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: PREOP_STAGING
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: When preoperative staging may be inaccurate
Guideline Action: Discuss potential inaccuracies of preoperative testing on tumor staging with the patient to support informed decision-making.
Source Statement: Potential inaccuracies of preoperative testing on tumour staging should be discussed with patients to allow them to make informed decisions (1).

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: PREOP_STAGING
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: When planning rectal surgery after preoperative therapy
Guideline Action: Use total mesorectal excision (TME) principles for the eventual rectal surgery.
Source Statement: The eventual rectal surgery is expected to include total mesorectal excision (TME) principles.

patient_vignette: A 52-year-old man in Ontario presents with a newly diagnosed, biopsy-proven undifferentiated nasopharyngeal carcinoma. Staging MRI and PET-CT show a stage IVB locally advanced primary tumor with bilateral cervical nodal involvement but no distant metastases. He has good performance status, normal renal and hepatic function, and is considered chemotherapy-eligible. The oncology team plans induction chemotherapy followed by definitive chemoradiotherapy. He understands the treatment will be coordinated closely because the timing of the transition to radiation is important after induction therapy.

rules_text:
Rule ID: R001
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: newly diagnosed, chemotherapy-eligible, locally advanced squamous cell or undifferentiated nasopharyngeal cancer (stage III or IV)
Guideline Action: Use chemoradiotherapy-based management with consideration of adding neoadjuvant, concurrent, or adjuvant chemotherapy as addressed in the guideline
Source Statement: The objectives of the guideline are to make recommendations regarding the addition of neoadjuvant/concurrent/adjuvant chemotherapy to chemoradiotherapy in the management of locally advanced squamous cell or undifferentiated nasopharyngeal cancer (NPC).

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: patients with NPC receiving induction chemotherapy
Guideline Action: Administer induction chemotherapy every 3 weeks for 3 cycles; at minimum give 2 cycles
Source Statement: For patients with NPC receiving induction chemotherapy, the regimens should be administered every three weeks for a total of three cycles, or at the minimum two cycles.

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: patients with NPC receiving induction chemotherapy
Guideline Action: Start chemoradiotherapy within 21 to 28 days from the first day of the last induction chemotherapy cycle
Source Statement: For patients with NPC receiving induction chemotherapy, chemoradiotherapy should be commenced within 21-28 days from the first day of the last cycle of induction chemotherapy.

Rule ID: R004
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: all patients with NPC receiving adjuvant chemotherapy
Guideline Action: Offer PF every 4 weeks for a total of 3 cycles
Source Statement: For all patients with NPC receiving adjuvant chemotherapy, PF ... administered every four weeks for a total of three cycles should be offered.

Rule ID: R005
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: patients with locally advanced NPC treated in Ontario context
Guideline Action: Apply the endorsed CSCO/ASCO recommendations as modified by Ontario Health endorsement
Source Statement: The Chemotherapy and Radiotherapy for Nasopharyngeal Cancer Development Group (GDG) of Ontario Health (Cancer Care Ontario) endorses the Chinese Society of Clinical Oncology (CSCO)/American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) recommendations ... modified by the endorsement process described in this document.

Rule ID: R006
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: patients with NPC receiving induction chemotherapy
Guideline Action: Use a 3-week cycle interval for induction chemotherapy
Source Statement: For patients with NPC receiving induction chemotherapy, the regimens should be administered every three weeks for a total of three cycles, or at the minimum two cycles.

Rule ID: R007
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: patients with NPC receiving adjuvant chemotherapy
Guideline Action: Use a 4-week cycle interval for PF adjuvant chemotherapy
Source Statement: For all patients with NPC receiving adjuvant chemotherapy, PF ... administered every four weeks for a total of three cycles should be offered.

Rule ID: R008
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: patients with NPC receiving induction chemotherapy followed by chemoradiotherapy
Guideline Action: Do not delay chemoradiotherapy beyond 28 days after the first day of the last induction cycle
Source Statement: For patients with NPC receiving induction chemotherapy, chemoradiotherapy should be commenced within 21-28 days from the first day of the last cycle of induction chemotherapy.

patient_vignette: A 25-year-old woman presents to discuss breast cancer screening. She was treated for Hodgkin lymphoma at age 18 with mantle radiation totaling 30 Gy, and her current risk assessment places her in risk category 5. She has no breast symptoms and is anxious because a relative was recently diagnosed with breast cancer. She asks whether she should begin screening now, since she has heard that high-risk women need early imaging. Because of his age, they consider whether to intensify treatment, add etoposide, or use a compressed 14-day schedule with growth factor support. Source Statement: There is insufficient evidence to support the routine use of granulocyte-colony stimulating factor as primary therapy.

Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80

Source Statement: No benefits from fractionating the treatment schedule have been detected; the potential for outcomes to be inferior is suggested.

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80

Guideline Action: Avoid CHOEP-14 because of excessive toxicity
Source Statement: patients receiving CHOEP every 14 days experienced excessive toxicity

Rule ID: R004
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: considering CHOP plus etoposide versus CHOP alone in older patients
Guideline Action: Do not add etoposide routinely to CHOP
Source Statement: No differences were detected in response rate, TTF, or OS, and the authors commented that the addition of etoposide was associated with significant toxicity.

Rule ID: R005
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: considering more intensive regimens than CHOP

patient_vignette: A 64-year-old man with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer completed first-line etoposide-cisplatin 5 months ago and had a partial response with marked symptom improvement. He now returns with worsening cough, weight loss, and new right hilar enlargement on CT, consistent with relapsed disease. His treatment-free interval is just over 5 months. He has mild residual peripheral neuropathy from prior cisplatin but remains ambulatory, independent in activities of daily living, and has an ECOG performance status of 1. He is interested in further treatment and asks about options. Because he previously responded and the relapse occurred more than 3 months after completion of chemotherapy, retreatment with the same regimen is being considered, along with other second-line options. Oral topotecan is also discussed as an alternative, since he responded initially and his response lasted longer than 45 days.

Rule ID: R001
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: adult patient with relapsed SCLC
Guideline Action: Consider second-line chemotherapy only after weighing treatment-free interval, response to first-line therapy, residual toxicity, and performance status.
Source Statement: The selection of patients for treatment with second-line therapy should be dependent on the treatment-free interval, the extent of response to first-line therapy, residual toxicity from first-line therapy, and the performance status of the patient.

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: patient relapses three or more months after completion of first-line chemotherapy
Guideline Action: Consider retreatment with the same regimen that produced the initial response, generally etoposide-cisplatin.
Source Statement: patients who relapse three or more months following the completion of first-line chemotherapy may benefit from retreatment with the same regimen that induced their initial response. This would generally mean retreatment with etoposide-cisplatin.

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: patient relapses three or more months after completion of first-line chemotherapy
Guideline Action: Consider alternative regimens such as CAV or carboplatin plus etoposide.
Source Statement: Alternative regimens may include cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, and vincristine (CAV) or carboplatin and etoposide.

Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: patient initially responded to chemotherapy and response duration was 45 days or longer

Source Statement: Oral topotecan is a possible alternative for patients who initially responded to chemotherapy and had a response duration of 45 days or longer.

patient_vignette: A 67-year-old man with inoperable stage IV colorectal adenocarcinoma presents to discuss first-line systemic therapy. He has liver and lung metastases, good performance status, and no prior chemotherapy. Rule ID: R001
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: Adult patient with inoperable, advanced stage IV colorectal cancer being considered for first-line systemic therapy
Guideline Action: Discuss intermittent systemic treatment strategies as a reasonable alternative to continuous administration as part of informed treatment decision-making
Source Statement: Intermittent systemic treatment strategies should be part of an informed discussion of treatment options for this group of patients.

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: Adult patient with unresectable metastatic colorectal cancer wants a break from treatment
Guideline Action: Reassure the patient that intermittent first-line therapy is a reasonable alternative to continuous therapy
Source Statement: Patients who want a break from treatment can be reassured that intermittent strategies of administering first-line therapy are a reasonable alternative to continuous administration.

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: Adult patient with unresectable metastatic colorectal cancer is considering intermittent versus continuous first-line systemic therapy
Guideline Action: Use intermittent therapy as an option because it does not show a statistically significant reduction in overall survival compared with continuous therapy
Source Statement: Meta-analysis demonstrates no clinically significant survival difference between the continuous and intermittent chemotherapy strategies (HR, 1.02; 95%CI, 0.95-1.10, p=0.62).

Rule ID: R004
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: Adult patient with unresectable metastatic colorectal cancer is considering intermittent versus continuous first-line systemic therapy
Guideline Action: Consider intermittent therapy because it may improve or maintain quality of life compared with continuous therapy
Source Statement: Intermittent strategies of administering first-line systemic therapies to patients with unresectable metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) do not result in a statistically significant reduction in overall survival and either improve or maintain quality of life compared to continuous administration of therapy.

Scenario: GENERAL

Guideline Action: Continue best supportive care

patient_vignette: A 27-year-old woman presents for a routine primary care visit and asks whether she should have a Pap test. Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: woman is younger than 21 years old
Guideline Action: Do not screen routinely.

Scenario: GENERAL

Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70

patient_vignette: A 52-year-old woman with a newly diagnosed left breast invasive ductal carcinoma presents to discuss surgery. Imaging shows a 4.2 cm tumor with biopsy-proven axillary lymph node involvement. The breast surgeon recommends mastectomy, and the patient is interested in immediate reconstruction if feasible. Because she is node-positive and is expected to receive postoperative radiation, the surgical team reviews reconstruction options carefully. On exam, there is no clinical skin or nipple-areolar complex involvement, and she has no history of Paget disease. She has already had diagnostic mammography and breast MRI for staging. A multidisciplinary visit is arranged to coordinate surgical, reconstructive, and radiation planning before finalizing the operative approach.

patient_vignette: A 64-year-old woman with high-grade serous epithelial ovarian cancer presents with symptomatic recurrence 5 months after completing her last platinum-based regimen. She has received three prior anticancer regimens and now has increasing abdominal discomfort, early satiety, and a CT scan showing peritoneal progression without bowel obstruction. Her disease is therefore platinum-resistant and she is not eligible for the AURELIA trial criteria because she has had more than two prior anticancer regimens. She asks about the next treatment steps and whether the goal is cure.

rules_text:
Rule ID: R001
Scenario: TREATMENT_RESPONSE
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: platinum-resistant recurrent ovarian cancer and not eligible for the AURELIA trial criteria
Guideline Action: Do not apply the bevacizumab plus chemotherapy option described for AURELIA-eligible patients.
Source Statement: Ineligible patients include those who have received >2 prior anticancer regimens or who had refractory disease, patients with a history of bowel obstruction (including subocclusive disease) related to underlying disease, a history of abdominal fistula, gastrointestinal perforation, or intra-abdominal abscess, or evidence of rectosigmoid involvement by pelvic examination, bowel involvement on computed tomography, or clinical symptoms of bowel obstruction.

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: all patients with recurrent epithelial ovarian cancer
Guideline Action: Assess each patient individually for recurrence status, platinum sensitivity, toxicity, ease of administration, and patient preference; recognize systemic therapy is not curative.
Source Statement: Systemic therapy for recurrent ovarian cancer is not curative. As such, it is recognized that, to determine the optimal therapy, each patient needs to be assessed individually in terms of recurrence, sensitivity to platinum, toxicity, ease of administration, and patient preference.

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: all patients with recurrent epithelial ovarian cancer
Guideline Action: Offer participation in clinical trials if appropriate.
Source Statement: All patients should be offered the opportunity to participate in clinical trials, if appropriate.

Rule ID: R004
Scenario: TREATMENT_RESPONSE
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer and a single platinum agent is not being considered because of toxicity or allergy
Guideline Action: Use monotherapy with paclitaxel, topotecan, or pegylated liposomal doxorubicin.
Source Statement: If a single platinum agent is not being considered (e.g., because of toxicity or allergy), then monotherapy with paclitaxel, topotecan, or pegylated liposomal doxorubicin is a reasonable treatment option.

Rule ID: R005
Scenario: TREATMENT_RESPONSE
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer with known BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation, somatic or germline, after platinum-based chemotherapy for recurrent disease
Guideline Action: Use PARP inhibitor maintenance treatment post platinum-based chemotherapy.
Source Statement: PARP inhibitors are recommended for patients with known BRCA 1 or 2 mutation (somatic and germline) as maintenance treatment post platinum-based chemotherapy for recurrent disease.

Rule ID: R006
Scenario: TREATMENT_RESPONSE
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: platinum-refractory or platinum-resistant recurrent ovarian cancer
Guideline Action: Set treatment goals to improving quality of life by extending symptom-free interval, reducing symptom intensity, increasing progression-free interval, or prolonging life if possible.
Source Statement: Lower levels of response to treatment are expected for this group; therefore, the goals of treatment should be to improve patient's quality of life by extending the symptom-free interval, reducing symptom intensity, increasing progression-free interval, or if possible, prolonging life.

Rule ID: R007
Scenario: TREATMENT_RESPONSE
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: platinum-refractory or platinum-resistant recurrent ovarian cancer
Guideline Action: Use single-agent paclitaxel, topotecan, pegylated liposomal doxorubicin, or gemcitabine as reasonable treatment options.
Source Statement: Single-agent paclitaxel, topotecan, pegylated liposomal doxorubicin, and gemcitabine have demonstrated activity in this patient population and are reasonable treatment options.

Rule ID: R008
Scenario: TREATMENT_RESPONSE
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer
Guideline Action: Offer chemotherapy with biologics after discussing the safety profile.
Source Statement: Women with platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer should be offered chemotherapy with biologics after a discussion concerning the safety profile

patient_vignette: A 29-year-old man who has sex with men presents for HIV prevention counseling. He reports multiple male partners over the past 6 months, inconsistent condom use, and one recent bacterial STI. He has no fever, rash, sore throat, or other symptoms suggestive of acute HIV infection, and he had a negative HIV test 2 weeks ago. He asks about starting PrEP and wonders whether he can take it only on days he expects sex, or whether he should add another antiretroviral medication for extra protection. He is otherwise healthy and has normal renal function. After discussing options, he is interested in daily PrEP and agrees to follow-up testing.

Rule ID: R001
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: child aged 2 through 4 years with asthma, recurrent wheezing, or wheezing/asthma in the past 12 months
Guideline Action: Do not give FluMist.

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: person caring for severely immunosuppressed persons who require a protective environment
Guideline Action: Do not give FluMist / LAIV.
Source Statement: Persons who care for severely immunosuppressed persons who require a protective environment should not receive FluMist given the theoretical risk for transmission of the live-attenuated vaccine virus.

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: child aged under 9 years
Guideline Action: Do not use Afluria.

Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: person with a previous severe allergic reaction to influenza vaccine
Guideline Action: Do not give future influenza vaccine.

Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED

rules_text:
Rule ID: R001
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: workplace exposure is to inorganic lead
Guideline Action: Control employee exposure by adhering to the standard sections in this document.
Source Statement: recommends that employee exposure to inorganic lead in the workplace be controlled by adherence to the following sections.

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: workplace exposure is to inorganic lead
Guideline Action: Apply the standard as a lifetime 8-hour day, 40-hour week protection target.
Source Statement: The standard is designed to protect the health and safety of workers for an 8-hour day, 40-hour week over a working lifetime; compliance with the standard should therefore prevent adverse effects of lead on the health and safety of workers.

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: workplace exposure is to inorganic lead
Guideline Action: Use valid, reproducible, and available measurement techniques for compliance determinations.
Source Statement: The standard is measurable by techniques that are valid, reproducible, and available to industry and government agencies.

Rule ID: R004
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: workplace exposure is to inorganic lead
Guideline Action: Recognize that sufficient technology exists to comply with the recommended standard.
Source Statement: Sufficient technology exists to permit compliance with the recommended standard.

Rule ID: R005
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: workplace air exposure to inorganic lead
Guideline Action: Keep the 8-hour time-weighted average airborne lead concentration at or below 0.15 mg Pb/m^3.
Source Statement: workers shall not be exposed to inorganic lead at a concentration greater that 0.15 mg Pb/m^ determined as a time-weighted average (TWA) exposure for an 8-hour workday.

Rule ID: R006
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: environmental samples are collected for lead monitoring
Guideline Action: Collect environmental samples using Appendix I or an equivalent method, and analyze them using Appendix II or an equivalent method with comparable precision and accuracy.
Source Statement: Procedures for collection of environmental samples shall be as provided in Appendix I, or by an equivalent method. Analysis of samples shall be as provided in Appendix II, or by any method shown to be equivalent in precision and accuracy to the method specified in Appendix II.

Rule ID: R007
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: worker is subject to exposure to inorganic lead
Guideline Action: Make biologic monitoring available to the worker.
Source Statement: Biologic monitoring shall be made available to all workers subject to "exposure to inorganic lead."

Rule ID: R008
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: worker is subject to exposure to inorganic lead
Guideline Action: Use whole blood lead testing, or urine lead testing as an alternative, to assess lead absorption.
Source Statement: It consists of sampling and analysis of whole blood, or alternatively, of urine for lead content.

patient_vignette: A 34-year-old elementary school teacher comes to urgent care after hearing that several students in her district developed sudden vomiting and diarrhea within the same day. She is visibly anxious and says parents are “panicking” on social media, asking whether the school cafeteria food was contaminated and whether this could be a deliberate poisoning. She has no fever or abdominal tenderness and is mainly worried about what to tell her family and coworkers. In the waiting room, she repeatedly asks for confirmation that the outbreak is “probably nothing serious” and wants to know the exact cause immediately. The clinic has not yet received confirmed public health information, and local officials are still investigating the source and scope of the illness.

rules_text:
Rule ID: R001
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: When the public may be worried or outraged
Guideline Action: Do not dismiss outrage or tell people they should not be afraid.
Source Statement: Don't Dismiss Outrage. ... When people are afraid and worried, the worst thing to do is pretend that they're not. The second worst thing is to tell them they shouldn't be.

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: When giving reassurance during an early crisis
Guideline Action: Do not over-reassure or minimize the risk.
Source Statement: Don't over-reassure. ... Reassurance can backfire.

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: When the public or media ask about cause, blame, or liability early in the event
Guideline Action: Do not discuss liability, blame, or cause before the situation is contained.

patient_vignette: A 29-year-old warehouse worker presents to occupational health after a late-afternoon shift in a non-air-conditioned loading dock. He had been stacking boxes and moving pallets for about 90 minutes with only brief water breaks. On the site nurse’s check, his oral temperature is 38.4°C, and he reports marked fatigue, heavy sweating, and a throbbing headache. He says he feels better after resting indoors for 20 minutes, but the supervisor wants him to return to the dock to finish the shift. He is otherwise healthy and has no history of heat illness. The workplace had been unusually hot all day, and several coworkers were also complaining of the heat.

Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: heat exposure is prolonged or severe enough to cause body temperature above 38°C

Source Statement: Unacclimatized employees shall be acclimatized over a period of 6 days. rules_text:
Rule ID: R001
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: routine prevention of hepatitis A in the United States
Guideline Action: Implement routine hepatitis A vaccination for children nationwide.
Source Statement: All children should receive hepatitis A vaccine at age 1 year (i.e., 12-23 months).

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: state, county, or community already has a hepatitis A vaccination program for children aged 2-18 years
Guideline Action: Maintain the existing childhood hepatitis A vaccination program.
Source Statement: States, counties, and communities with existing hepatitis A vaccination programs for children aged 2-18 years are encouraged to maintain these programs.

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: person is traveling to or working in a country with high or intermediate hepatitis A endemicity and is susceptible
Guideline Action: Vaccinate before departure or give immune globulin before departure; vaccine is preferred.
Source Statement: All susceptible persons traveling to or working in countries that have high or intermediate hepatitis A endemicity (Figure 4) should be vaccinated or receive IG before departure (Tables 1-4). Hepatitis A vaccination at the age-appropriate dose is preferred (Tables 2-4).

Rule ID: R004
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: travel is planned and first vaccine dose can be given now
Guideline Action: Give the first hepatitis A vaccine dose as soon as travel is considered.
Source Statement: The first dose of hepatitis A vaccine should be administered as soon as travel is considered.

Rule ID: R005
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: traveler departs in less than 4 weeks and cannot or will not receive immune globulin
Guideline Action: Still give hepatitis A vaccine and inform the traveler protection may be incomplete for the next 2-4 weeks.
Source Statement: Travelers departing in <4 weeks who do not or cannot receive IG should nonetheless receive hepatitis A vaccine and be informed that they might not be optimally protected from acquiring hepatitis A in the immediate future (i.e., subsequent 2-4 weeks).

Rule ID: R006
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: traveler is allergic to a vaccine component or declines vaccine
Guideline Action: Give a single dose of immune globulin 0.02 mL/kg; if travel lasts more than 2 months, use 0.06 mL/kg and repeat if travel lasts more than 5 months.
Source Statement: Travelers who are allergic to a vaccine component or who elect not to receive vaccine should receive a single dose of IG (0.02 mL/kg), which provides effective protection against hepatitis A for up to 3 months (Table 1). Travelers whose travel period is >2 months should be administered IG at 0.06 mL/kg; administration must be repeated if the travel period is >5 months (Table 1).

Rule ID: R007
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: person is an adolescent or adult man who has sex with men
Guideline Action: Vaccinate against hepatitis A.
Source Statement: MSM (both adolescents and adults) should be vaccinated.

Rule ID: R008
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: person uses injection or noninjection illicit drugs
Guideline Action: Vaccinate against hepatitis A.
Source Statement: Vaccination is recommended for users of injection and noninjection illicit drugs.

patient_vignette: A 15-year-old student is brought to a school health planning meeting after the district notices inconsistent food practices across campuses. The middle school is drafting a new nutrition policy because vending machines, classroom celebrations, and fundraisers currently vary by teacher and club. Parents have asked for healthier options, while students want foods that fit cultural preferences and after-school sports schedules. The school nurse reports that some teachers use candy as rewards, and the PTA is considering a fundraiser built around soda and chips. Administrators want a policy that can be rolled out this semester but also updated after feedback from families, staff, and students. The team is looking for a practical plan that supports healthy eating without ignoring local food traditions or the needs of different student groups.

patient_vignette: A 58-year-old postmenopausal woman is seen after lumpectomy for a 1.8 cm invasive ductal carcinoma. Pathology shows ER-positive, HER2-negative disease with 2 of 12 axillary lymph nodes involved, no distant metastases, and intermediate grade. She is otherwise healthy and is anxious to avoid chemotherapy if it would not add meaningful benefit. The team plans to use the result for this single treatment decision and does not intend to send multiple different assays on the same specimen.

He has recovered well after surgery and is asking whether he should start chemotherapy to reduce recurrence risk. His oncology team is reviewing the pathology and discussing postoperative management. The pathology report also notes that the tumor is mismatch repair proficient, and this result was obtained before the postoperative visit.

Rule ID: R001
Scenario: INITIAL_DIAGNOSIS
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: adult patient with resected stage II colon cancer
Guideline Action: Do not use routine adjuvant chemotherapy for all stage II patients.
Source Statement: The routine use of adjuvant chemotherapy for all patients with stage II colon cancer is not recommended.

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: INITIAL_DIAGNOSIS
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: stage II patient without high-risk features who does not require adjuvant chemotherapy
Guideline Action: Do not perform MSI/dMMR testing for this decision.
Source Statement: In stage II (in the absence of high-risk features) where a patient does not require adjuvant chemotherapy, MSI/dMMR testing is not recommended as it will not influence that decision.

Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: stage II colon cancer with MSI/dMMR after surgery
Guideline Action: Do not give fluoropyrimidine monotherapy as adjuvant treatment.
Source Statement: Adjuvant chemotherapy with a fluoropyrimidine monotherapy regimen following surgery in patients who have MSI/dMMR is not recommended.

Scenario: INITIAL_DIAGNOSIS
Priority: 70

Priority: 80

Guideline Action: Do not use induction chemotherapy as standard care; treat it as investigational only.
Source Statement: At this time, induction CT before concurrent CT and RT should be considered an investigational approach.

Scenario: INITIAL_DIAGNOSIS
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: NSCLC patient has not had mutation testing or is only clinically selected by ethnicity, sex, histology, or smoking status
Guideline Action: Do not use first-line EGFR TKI therapy based on clinical selection alone
Source Statement: First-line therapy with an EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) is not recommended in unselected (patients who have not undergone mutation testing) or clinically selected populations of patients.

Source Statement: The use of clinical characteristics such as Asian ethnicity, female sex, adenocarcinoma histology and light/never smoking status is not recommended to select patients for first-line EGFR TKI therapy, as this strategy does not reliably select patients who have mutations.

Source Statement: Two randomized phase II trials ... identified that grade 3 or 4 toxicity was higher with the higher dose gefitinib. Interstitial lung disease-type events occurred in only one of the two trials, and only with 500 mg/day gefitinib.

Rule ID: R001
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: patient has stage IIIA, IIIB, IIIC, IIID, or resected IV melanoma and is being screened for asymptomatic recurrence or metastatic disease
Guideline Action: do not order routine biomarker or blood tests for screening
Source Statement: 3.2 Routine biomarker or blood tests to screen for asymptomatic recurrence or metastatic disease are not recommended.

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: patient has stage IA, IB, or IIA melanoma and is clinically disease-free after curative-intent treatment
Guideline Action: perform clinical follow-up with history and physical examination including full skin and lymph node examination every 6 to 12 months for 3 years, then annually for 2 years or as clinically indicated; dermatologist, surgeon, family physician, or cancer nurse specialist may provide follow-up; photo-surveillance and dermoscopy if indicated
Source Statement: For patients with stage IA, IB, or IIA melanoma who are clinically disease-free after receiving curative-intent treatment: 1.1 Clinical follow-up with history and physical examination with full skin and lymph node examination by a dermatologist (with photo-surveillance and dermoscopy if indicated), and/or a surgeon, family physician, cancer nurse specialists should occur every six to 12 months for three years, then annually for two years or as clinically indicated.

Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70

Activation Condition: patient has stage IIIA, IIIB, IIIC, IIID, or resected IV melanoma
Guideline Action: perform clinical follow-up with history and physical examination including full skin and lymph node examination every 3 to 6 months in years 1 to 3, then every 6 months in years 4 to 5, or as clinically indicated; dermatologist, surgeon, medical oncologist, or cancer nurse specialist may provide follow-up; photo-surveillance and dermoscopy if indicated
Source Statement: For patients with stage IIIA, IIIB, IIIC, IIID, or resected IV melanoma: 3.1 Clinical follow-up with history and physical examination with full skin and lymph node examination by a dermatologist (with photo-surveillance and dermoscopy if indicated), and/or a surgeon, medical oncologist, or cancer nurse specialist should occur every three to six months in years 1 to 3, then every six months in years 4 to 5, or as clinically indicated.

She feels well and denies weight loss, headaches, cough, bone pain, new skin lesions, or neurologic symptoms. Physical examination shows a healed scar, no palpable lymphadenopathy, and no concerning skin findings. She asks whether she should have blood tests or an ultrasound of the groin to check for recurrence because she remains anxious about metastatic disease. She is otherwise healthy and asymptomatic.

rules_text:
Rule ID: R001
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: patient has stage IIIA, IIIB, IIIC, IIID, or resected IV melanoma and is being screened for asymptomatic recurrence or metastatic disease
Guideline Action: do not order routine biomarker or blood tests for screening
Source Statement: 3.2 Routine biomarker or blood tests to screen for asymptomatic recurrence or metastatic disease are not recommended.

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: patient has stage IA, IB, or IIA melanoma and is clinically disease-free after curative-intent treatment
Guideline Action: perform clinical follow-up with history and physical examination including full skin and lymph node examination every 6 to 12 months for 3 years, then annually for 2 years or as clinically indicated; dermatologist, surgeon, family physician, or cancer nurse specialist may provide follow-up; photo-surveillance and dermoscopy if indicated
Source Statement: For patients with stage IA, IB, or IIA melanoma who are clinically disease-free after receiving curative-intent treatment: 1.1 Clinical follow-up with history and physical examination with full skin and lymph node examination by a dermatologist (with photo-surveillance and dermoscopy if indicated), and/or a surgeon, family physician, cancer nurse specialists should occur every six to 12 months for three years, then annually for two years or as clinically indicated.

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: patient has stage IIIA, IIIB, IIIC, IIID, or resected IV melanoma
Guideline Action: perform clinical follow-up with history and physical examination including full skin and lymph node examination every 3 to 6 months in years 1 to 3, then every 6 months in years 4 to 5, or as clinically indicated; dermatologist, surgeon, medical oncologist, or cancer nurse specialist may provide follow-up; photo-surveillance and dermoscopy if indicated
Source Statement: For patients with stage IIIA, IIIB, IIIC, IIID, or resected IV melanoma: 3.1 Clinical follow-up with history and physical examination with full skin and lymph node examination by a dermatologist (with photo-surveillance and dermoscopy if indicated), and/or a surgeon, medical oncologist, or cancer nurse specialist should occur every three to six months in years 1 to 3, then every six months in years 4 to 5, or as clinically indicated.

Rule ID: R004
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: brain MRI is being used for routine screening and is available
Guideline Action: prefer MRI of the brain without radiation
Source Statement: MRI (no radiation) of the brain is preferred for routine screening where available, otherwise, head CT may be considered after discussing with patients.

Rule ID: R005
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: patient has a positive sentinel lymph node and no complete lymph node dissection was performed
Guideline Action: perform ultrasound scans of the draining nodal basin every 4 to 6 months for years 1 to 3, then every 6 months for years 4 to 5
Source Statement: 3.5 For patients with a positive sentinel lymph node, ultrasound scans of the draining nodal basin should be done every four to six months for years 1 to 3, and then every six months for years 4 to 5, if no complete lymph node dissection is performed.

Rule ID: R006
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: patient has stage IIIA, IIIB, IIIC, IIID, or resected IV melanoma and is being screened for asymptomatic recurrence or metastatic disease in years 1 to 3
Guideline Action: consider CT or PET/CT scans every 6 to 12 months
Source Statement: 3.3 CT or PET/CT scans every six to 12 months should be considered to screen for asymptomatic recurrence or metastatic disease in years 1 to 3, then annually in years 4 to 5.

Rule ID: R007
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: patient has stage IIIA, IIIB, IIIC, IIID, or resected IV melanoma and is being screened for asymptomatic recurrence or metastatic disease in years 4 to 5
Guideline Action: consider CT or PET/CT scans annually
Source Statement: 3.3 CT or PET/CT scans every six to 12 months should be considered to screen for asymptomatic recurrence or metastatic disease in years 1 to 3, then annually in years 4 to 5.

Rule ID: R008
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: patient has stage IIIA, IIIB, IIIC, IIID, or resected IV melanoma
Guideline Action: consider annual brain MRI for years 1 to 5
Source Statement: 3.4 Annual brain MRI can be considered for years 1 to 5.

patient_vignette: A 64-year-old woman is seen in oncology follow-up 8 months after undergoing total hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy for stage IB, grade 2 endometrioid endometrial cancer. Final pathology showed no residual disease outside the uterus, and she has no current evidence of disease. She reports feeling well overall and denies vaginal bleeding, pelvic pain, new cough, weight loss, or bowel or bladder changes. She completed treatment without radiotherapy. She asks what follow-up should include and who should see her. She is anxious about recurrence and wants to know which symptoms should prompt an earlier visit.

rules_text:
Rule ID: R001
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: all patients with endometrial cancer after potentially curative primary treatment and no evidence of disease
Guideline Action: counsel about potential symptoms of recurrence
Source Statement: It is recommended that all patients receive counselling about the potential symptoms of recurrence of endometrial cancer, because the majority of recurrences in the identified studies were symptomatic.

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: patient is surgically or pathologically confirmed low risk of recurrence (stage IA or IB, grade 1 or 2)
Guideline Action: perform general examination including complete history and pelvic-rectal examination semi-annually or annually for the first 3 years, then annually for the next 2 years
Source Statement: For patients at a surgically or pathologically confirmed low risk of recurrence (i.e., stage IA or IB, grade 1 or 2): A general examination, including a complete history and a pelvicrectal examination, conducted semi-annually or annually for the first three years and annually for the next two years.

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: patient is high risk of recurrence (stage IA or IB, grade 3, or stage IC or advanced stage)
Guideline Action: perform general examination including complete history and pelvic-rectal examination every 3 to 6 months for the first 3 years, then semi-annually for the next 2 years
Source Statement: For patients at high risk of recurrence (i.e., stage IA or IB, grade 3, or stage IC or advanced stage). A general examination, including a complete history and a pelvic-rectal examination, every three to six months for the first three years and semi-annually for the next two years.

Rule ID: R004
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: planning follow-up setting or specialist type for any patient
Guideline Action: follow the patient with a health care professional knowledgeable about the natural history of the disease and comfortable performing speculum and pelvic exams
Source Statement: There is insufficient evidence to inform the optimum clinical setting or type of specialist required for follow-up; however, it is recommended that all patients be followed by a health care professional who is knowledgeable about the natural history of the disease, and who is comfortable performing speculum and pelvic exams, in order to diagnose or detect a local (vaginal) recurrence.

Rule ID: R005
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: patient has symptoms suggestive of recurrence
Guideline Action: perform targeted investigation to rule out recurrence
Source Statement: It is recommended that all patients undergo a targeted investigation to rule out recurrence if symptomatic, since patients with local recurrence are potentially curable with further therapy.

Rule ID: R006
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: treatment includes radiotherapy
Guideline Action: counsel the patient on potential adverse effects of radiotherapy
Source Statement: Where treatment with radiotherapy is involved, it is recommended that patients be counselled on the potential adverse effects of radiotherapy.

Rule ID: R007
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: all patients with endometrial cancer after potentially curative primary treatment and no evidence of disease
Guideline Action: use a follow-up strategy based on recurrence risk and patient preferences
Source Statement: The most appropriate follow-up strategy is likely one based upon the risk of recurrence, with individual patient preferences for more or less follow-up taken into account.

Rule ID: R008
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: patient has remained recurrence-free for 5 years
Guideline Action: return to annual population-based general physical and pelvic examination
Source Statement: Since the majority of patients with recurrence were symptomatic and virtually all recurred within five years, it seems reasonable that patients return to annual population-based general physical and pelvic examination after five years of recurrence-free follow-up.

- Use a follow-up strategy based on recurrence risk and the patient’s preferences.

rules_text:
Rule ID: R001
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: patient is receiving alemtuzumab consolidation after response to first-line fludarabine-containing chemotherapy
Guideline Action: Avoid routine consolidation with alemtuzumab because the trial was stopped early for severe infections
Source Statement: The trial was stopped after the accrual of 21 patients due to the occurrence of the National Cancer Institute Common Toxicity Criteria (NCI-CTC) Version 2.0 grade III/IV infections in seven of the first 11 patients randomized to alemtuzumab consolidation.

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: adult patient with progressive and symptomatic CLL refractory to both alkylator-based and fludarabine-based regimens
Guideline Action: Consider alemtuzumab as a reasonable treatment option
Source Statement: Treatment with alemtuzumab is a reasonable option for patients with progressive and symptomatic CLL that is refractory to both alkylator-based and fludarabine-based regimens.

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: patient was previously treated with alkylating agents and is refractory to fludarabine without bulky lymphadenopathy
Guideline Action: Consider alemtuzumab
Source Statement: the UK CLL Forum guideline recommended alemtuzumab for use in patients without bulky lymphadenopathy (<5cm), who were previously treated with alkylating agents and refractory to fludarabine.

Rule ID: R004
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: considering alemtuzumab for CLL
Guideline Action: Inform the patient that evidence for benefit on duration of response, quality of life, and overall survival is not established and remains speculative
Source Statement: Patients should be informed that any possible beneficial effect of alemtuzumab on other outcome measures such as duration of response, quality of life, and overall survival are not supported in evidence and remain speculative at this time.

Rule ID: R005
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: considering alemtuzumab for CLL
Guideline Action: Inform the patient that treatment has significant and potentially serious toxicities and that the balance of harm versus benefit is uncertain
Source Statement: Treatment with alemtuzumab is associated with significant and potentially serious adverse treatment-related toxicities. Patients must be carefully informed of the uncertain balance between potential risks of harm and the chance for benefit reported in studies.

Rule ID: R006
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: considering alemtuzumab for CLL
Guideline Action: Use patient preferences as an important factor in deciding whether to treat
Source Statement: Given the current substantial uncertainty in this balance, patient preferences will likely play a large role in determining the appropriate treatment choice.

Rule ID: R007
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: patient has important co-morbidities
Guideline Action: Use alemtuzumab cautiously because excessive risk may be present
Source Statement: Given the potential toxicities associated with alemtuzumab, and given the limited nature of the clinical trials testing its use in broad populations of patients with CLL, the use of alemtuzumab in patients with important co-morbidities may be associated with excessive risks.

Rule ID: R008
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: patient has relapsed or chemotherapy-refractory CLL
Guideline Action: Recognize alemtuzumab as an active agent that can produce responses, but note that complete remissions are uncommon
Source Statement: The DSG regards alemtuzumab as an active agent for the treatment of patients with relapsed or chemotherapy-refractory CLL. This conclusion is based on response data from single-arm studies that report partial responses in approximately one third of patients and recognizes that complete remissions are uncommon.

patient_vignette: A 58-year-old man with primary systemic AL amyloidosis presents after 5 months of bortezomib-based therapy with partial hematologic response. He has persistent nephrotic-range proteinuria and mild peripheral edema, but no symptomatic heart failure. Echocardiography shows preserved ejection fraction with mild concentric thickening, and his creatinine is stable at 1.1 mg/dL. He remains active, works full-time, and wants the most aggressive treatment that offers the best chance of long-term disease control. His hematologist discusses stem cell transplantation as a next step. Because he has AL amyloidosis and is being evaluated for SCT, the team reviews his organ involvement, overall functional status, comorbidities, and treatment goals before deciding whether he is an appropriate transplant candidate.

Guideline Action: Do not use re-irradiation

Scenario: INITIAL_DIAGNOSIS
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: Adult patient with previously untreated early (T1) glottic cancer

Scenario: INITIAL_DIAGNOSIS
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: Adult patient with previously untreated early (T1) glottic cancer
Guideline Action: Choose between surgery and radiation based on patient and clinician preferences and general medical condition

Scenario: INITIAL_DIAGNOSIS

Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER

Thoracic surgery feels he is an appropriate candidate for esophagectomy after neoadjuvant treatment. He has well-controlled hypertension and no major cardiopulmonary disease. In clinic, he asks whether he can proceed directly to surgery or if treatment before surgery would improve his chances. The oncology team is considering preoperative therapy options and discussing expected toxicities and the fact that any survival benefit may be modest. The patient says he values the best chance of cure but wants to understand how treatment might affect swallowing, fatigue, and recovery before making a decision.

The specimen is being processed in a licensed, accredited laboratory using paraffin-embedded tissue sections cut at 4 microns. Initial p16 immunohistochemical staining shows diffuse, moderate-to-strong cytoplasmic and nuclear staining in about 80% of tumour cells. The oncologist asks whether the HPV result should change the treatment plan immediately.

patient_vignette: A 67-year-old man is 18 months after lobectomy and adjuvant chemotherapy for stage II non-small cell lung cancer. His PSA has been stable around 5.1 ng/mL, his digital rectal exams have remained normal, and his confirmatory TRUS biopsy 3 years ago showed no upgrading. Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80

Scenario: GENERAL

Guideline Action: Repeat serial biopsy at least every 3 to 5 years.
Source Statement: The AS protocol should include the following tests: -12-to 14-core confirmatory transrectal ultrasound (TRUS) biopsy (including anterior directed cores) within 6 to 12 months, then serial biopsy a minimum of every 3 to 5 years thereafter.

Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: Patient on active surveillance has rapidly rising PSA, PSA density over 0.2, higher PSA than expected for prostate size, DRE abnormality, or very low PSA free/total ratio.
Guideline Action: Investigate further with mpMRI or earlier repeat biopsy.
Source Statement: Discordant findings between a patient's clinical course and pathologic findings can include rapidly rising PSA, PSA density over 0.2, higher PSA than expected for prostate size, DRE abnormality, and very low PSA free/total ratio. Presence of these findings requires further investigation with mpMRI or earlier repeat biopsy.

Scenario: GENERAL

Rule ID: R001
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: adult patient with relapsed SCLC
Guideline Action: Consider second-line chemotherapy only after weighing treatment-free interval, response to first-line therapy, residual toxicity, and performance status.

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: patient relapses three or more months after completion of first-line chemotherapy
Guideline Action: Consider retreatment with the same regimen that produced the initial response, generally etoposide-cisplatin.
Source Statement: patients who relapse three or more months following the completion of first-line chemotherapy may benefit from retreatment with the same regimen that induced their initial response. This would generally mean retreatment with etoposide-cisplatin.

Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80

Activation Condition: When considering limited ACP implementation

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80

Activation Condition: When using education alone to improve ACP care
Guideline Action: Do not expect education alone to improve care or patient experience without supporting system changes.

Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: When considering whether pediatric ACP causes distress
Guideline Action: Do not assume ACP discussions increase distress in children or parents.

Rule ID: R004
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER

Guideline Action: Use a system-wide approach to integrate ACP into routine practice and maximize interprofessional team skills.

Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: When developing ACP tools or processes

Scenario: GENERAL
